get: verb
receive something
typical: get + letter/message/gift/call. NOT for: becoming (see become sense).
I got a message from Tom this morning.
She got a lovely present for her birthday.
verb
obtain or buy something
typical: get + object, where did you get it. NOT for: receiving unasked.
Where did you get that jacket?
I need to get some milk.
verb
bring or fetch someone or something
typical: get + object, get sb sth. NOT for: buying.
Can you get my glasses from the kitchen?
I'll get you a glass of water.
verb
arrive or reach a place or point
typical: get to/home/there/here. NOT for: obtaining things.
What time did you get home?
We got to the station late.
verb
become (a state)
typical: get + adjective: tired, angry, dark, better, worse. NOT for: receiving.
It gets dark early in winter.
He got angry when he heard the news.
verb
catch an illness
typical: get + flu/a cold/ill. NOT for: obtaining things.
I got flu last week.
She got a cold on holiday.
verb
understand something
typical: get it, get the joke/point. NOT for: physical receiving.
I don't think she got the joke.
Sorry, I don't get it. Can you explain?
verb
make or persuade someone to do something, or have something done
typical: get sb to do sth, get sth done. NOT for: forcing by strength (see make).
I got my brother to help me move.
We need to get this report finished.
verb
travel somewhere by a vehicle
typical: get a bus/train/taxi. NOT for: arriving at a point.
We'll get the 8:15 train.
I usually get a taxi home.
go: verb
travel or move to a place
typical: go to/into/out/home/abroad. NOT for: leaving as a single action (see leave) or becoming.
We go to the gym every Monday.
She went to Spain last summer.
verb
do an activity (go + -ing)
typical: go swimming/shopping/running/camping. NOT for: moving to a destination.
We went shopping on Saturday.
He goes running before work.
verb
attend a place regularly or for an event
typical: go to school/work/church/a concert. NOT for: one-off travel.
The children go to school at eight.
I'm going to a concert tonight.
verb
leave a place
typical: I must go now, time to go. NOT for: arriving.
I have to go now, my bus is here.
What time does the last train go?
verb
be going to: intend or be about to do something
typical: be going to + verb. NOT for: motion.
I'm going to call her tomorrow.
It's going to rain.
verb
become, usually something negative
typical: go bad/wrong/mad/quiet/grey. NOT for: positive changes.
The milk has gone bad.
His hair is starting to go grey.
verb
happen or develop in a certain way
typical: how did it go?, go well/badly. NOT for: travel.
How did the interview go?
Everything went well.
give: verb
let someone have something as a present or by handing it over
typical: give + person + thing, give sth to sb. NOT for: selling.
She gave me a present.
Give him the key.
verb
tell or provide information or help
typical: give advice/directions/instructions/an answer/details. NOT for: physical objects.
Can you give me directions to the station?
He gave us some useful advice.
verb
do an action expressed by the noun
typical: give a smile/wave/push/hug/try/look. NOT for: physical gifts.
She gave me a big hug.
Give it a try.
verb
make a speech, talk or performance
typical: give a talk/speech/lecture/concert. NOT for: gifts.
He gave a short speech at the wedding.
The band gave a concert in the park.
verb
make someone feel or experience something
typical: give sb a shock/headache/surprise/chance. NOT for: objects.
The noise gave me a headache.
The news gave us a shock.
verb
organize a party or social event
typical: give a party/dinner. NOT for: attending one.
They are giving a party on Saturday.
We gave a dinner for our neighbours.
verb
pay an amount of money for something
typical: give + money + for sth. NOT for: gifts.
I'll give you ten euros for it.
They gave £700 for the old car.
verb
allow an amount of time
typical: give sb time/a week/a few days. NOT for: giving objects.
Give me a few minutes to finish.
They gave us a week to decide.
